$comment: The sidebar's edge (--color-sidebar-border against the canvas) is deliberately NOT declared: WCAG 1.4.11 covers UI components and graphical objects needed to understand content, and a decorative separator beside a sidebar that already differs in background is neither. Declaring it would fail at ~1.2:1 in four themes and the only ways out would be darkening a decorative line everywhere or booking an allowance the ratchet may not grow. Token pairings the framework renders, as data, in two sections held to two different bars. `textPairs` are foreground/background pairs painted as TEXT and held to WCAG 2.1 AA for normal text; `nonTextPairs` are the visual boundaries and state indicators SC 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of — a focus indicator, the border that says which control is active, the outline of a control against its surface. Two consumers read both: tokens.contrast.test.js measures each pairing at its own bar, and the generated token manifest publishes them so a theme editor or an agent can tell which tokens must stay legible against which. A pair of token names appears in one section only: the text bar is the stricter of the two, so restating a text pairing under a non-text name would add a case that cannot fail unless the stricter one already has, and would overstate how much the ratchets cover. Purely decorative marks stay absent from both sections — WCAG sets no ratio for a divider or for an aria-hidden ornament, and asserting one would teach the next reader to ignore this file. Names are CSS custom properties because that is the vocabulary a theme author writes and a manifest consumer reads. A pairing earns its place here even when no specimen paints it, and two of them are exactly that: axe measures the pixels a lane renders, so a surface that only appears on a state no specimen can reach - a failed sign-in, a failed create - has no lane coverage at all, and the declared pairing is the only gate it will ever have.

textPairs.$comment: Subtle ink on the CANVAS, which is the half that was missing. Only the surface pairing was declared, and the two are not the same measurement once the canvas is tinted away from the surface: in light this reads 5.29:1 where the surface reads 6.13, and at the previous #64748b it was 4.20 against a canvas the surface pairing still passed at 4.76. Every consumer that sits on the page rather than in a card — the DataView toolbar's result count, a section's lead line — failed axe while the declared pairing stayed green, which is exactly the coverage claim this file exists to make honest.
textPairs.label: subtle text on the canvas

textPairs.$comment: The summary band's fill (ADR 0169 §4) and the three inks it carries: a figure's value and label, and the accent a figure's trend line and a link are drawn in. Its own token rather than the brand's soft tint read directly, because the record leaves the fill to the theme: a palette that wants a calmer band moves this one token, and the tint the hub tiles and the selected states share stays where it is. Every theme ships it at its soft tint. A figure's delta is not here: it is a pill with its own soft fill, held by the badge pairings wherever a band or a card puts it.

textPairs.$comment: The nav link's two raised states, which are one pairing: hover has painted sidebar-fg on sidebar-accent since the sidebar family was wired, and the active route joined it when its brand fill moved to neutral. It went undeclared through both, and the gap had teeth — the version of the active rule that kept accent ink on the same wash measured 4.07:1 in dark and 4.36 in twilight, and only the axe lane caught it, per specimen, at the end of a 26-minute run. Declared here it is arithmetic over five themes instead.

nonTextPairs.$comment: A Meter's fill against its track, which is the graphical object SC 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of: the fill's extent IS the value, and a fill that blends into its track is a bar that says nothing. Four pairings for the four fills the sheet paints — the unbanded accent and the three band tones — each against the one track they sit in. The track itself is not held against the page: it is a recess whose end the printed value makes redundant, and WCAG sets no ratio for that. The fill is --color-fg-accent rather than --color-brand-primary on purpose, and this file is where that choice is enforced: the brand fill measures 1.98 to 2.66 against this track in the three dark themes, because it is a surface for light text rather than a mark on the app's own ground.
nonTextPairs.label: a meter's fill against its track

nonTextPairs.$comment: A status column's dot (ADR 0169 §5), the graphical object SC 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of: it is the column's tone at a glance, and the text beside it is the word. Four pairings for the four toned dots; the neutral dot is the subtle ink, which the text pairing subtle-on-surface already holds to more than this.
